- For the second use case, you can find collection name as a first key in the array of the export.json file.
If you're still encountering problems in your use case, it would be great if you could send us your export.json file so we can help you solve them.
Thank you!

Hi alangornick1 ,
Yes. The swap rebinds layers/components to variables in the target collection, so links point to the published library variables (not local copies). Cross-file connections are preserved.
What it does/doesn’t:
* Preserves links if the target collection is from a published, accessible library.
* Relinks node bindings; it does not move/migrate variable definitions.
* Keeps component property bindings; mode context is preserved best‑effort (works best when mode names match across collections).
Caveats:
* Consumer files must have the target library enabled.
If helpful, share a minimal “tokens ↔ design system” pair and we’ll validate on your setup on figterate@gmail.com

Our license/trial server went down on 20 July (the host shut off that platform). That’s why the plugin has been unreliable for a lot of people: trials and paid access couldn’t load. We’ve moved licensing to a new server and are shipping an update. After you update, if you already bought, re-enter your Gumroad key once via Buy now. Trials reset to 0/10.

On your actual issue: variables copy but they’re not attached. That’s separate from the outage, and we don’t want you to buy until that works.

Can you tell us:

1. Was this Import from JSON or Swap between collections/libraries?
2. Do the new variables show in the Variables panel, but fills/text/spacing on layers stay unlinked?
3. Are you binding on main components, or instances? (Figma often blocks bindings on instance sublayers.)
4. For Swap: is the target local or a published library enabled in the file?

A screenshot (or the JSON if it’s import) helps a lot. Email figterate@gmail.com if that’s easier.

Thanks for being honest — we’ll get this sorted before you spend anything.
